scope: Offline analysis only. Original reports are preserved. Generic-row is contaminated and excluded only from the explicitly labeled nine-case diagnostic, not replaced or silently repaired in a ten-case result.

nineCaseDiagnostic.scope: Remaining nine measured cases only. Generic-row must be replicated; this is not a replacement full-ten result.

genericRow.status: contaminated; do not claim 46.4 percent improvement
genericRow.timelineCaveat: Timestamps are retained stdout filesystem mtimes, not measured process start/end timestamps. Row order and recorded process durations establish the serial sequence independently.
genericRow.finding: Fourth generic-row first before sample is 251 ms for 667 repetitions, agreeing with historical 250/250/251 ms and its own 256 ms pilot. Later before samples are 454/453 ms; C jumps from 320/321 to 631 ms; candidate jumps from 249/248 to 425 ms. Subsequent ray candidate/C pilots are slow and recover before timed rounds. This is a transient affecting multiple unchanged products; separate role medians select different performance regimes.
genericRow.resolution: All timed intervals are well above integer-millisecond resolution and accepted minimum duration. The ~1.7–2x transient cannot be explained by 1 ms quantization.
genericRow.environment: Both guards use taskset CPU3 and identical runtime options. CPU time tracks wall closely during slow samples, which weighs against ordinary off-CPU descheduling. Frequency, thermal, SMT/shared-resource pressure and host scheduling telemetry are not retained, so the physical cause remains unresolved.

thirdQbe.scope: Five-case screen versus first QBE candidate. Tree/map/record regressions are sustained across rotated samples; text/generic improve. No generic-row-like factor-of-two temporal instability is visible; this supports treating it as a mixed/negative candidate, without causal attribution to any one change.
